evidence.detail: The overlay renders a full-screen rectangle across Client width/height using color value 0 and a time-varying alpha, with no text, sprite or world-coordinate target.
Packet-controlled duration q is multiplied by 1000 ms; elapsed time is converted to a 0..255 alpha ramp and the overlay resets itself when the ramp reaches either bound.
Positive mode increases alpha from transparent toward opaque black; negative mode computes 255 minus the same ramp, producing the inverse fade from opaque black toward transparent.
The central rs/l/e/f overlay framework owns rs/l/e/a/k as its static h overlay and registers it during overlay initialization.

candidates.note: ScreenFadeOverlay is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for the full-screen black alpha-ramp overlay. It does not claim an original developer identifier; confidence is 0.998.

evidence.detail: R115 ScriptPacketDispatcher registers ScriptPacket ID 26 from rs/l/e/a/k.p; exact v308 initializes that field with concrete handler rs/l/e/a/l.
The handler reads exactly two integers. The first selects fade mode; packet value 2 is normalized to -1, otherwise the value is preserved. The second is the fade duration.
The handler delegates those two values only to rs/l/e/a/k.a(mode,duration), which stores fade direction/duration and resets the fade start timestamp.
No widget, Client gameplay state or second overlay is touched; the whole handler surface is the ScreenFadeOverlay transition control.

candidates.note: ScreenFadeOverlayPacketHandler is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for ScriptPacket 26. The handler only selects screen-fade direction and duration; confidence is 0.998.
